data.one_liner: An efficient, small mobile key-value storage framework.
data.what_it_does: MMKV uses mmap to keep memory synced with files and protobuf to encode/decode values, providing fast key-value storage. It supports primitive types, strings, bytes, multi-process concurrency, and optional encryption.
use_when: You need a high-performance key-value storage solution on mobile or desktop.
You require multi-process concurrent access to the same storage files.
avoid_when: You require complex relational queries, which are better suited for a SQL database.
You need built-in reactive streams for data observation.
strengths: Extremely efficient memory and file synchronization via mmap.
Small binary footprint and lightweight dependencies.
weaknesses: Must wait for MMKV initialization to finish before accessing instances.
Limited built-in data types compared to NoSQL document databases.
data.setup_notes: Call MMKV.initialize() in main() before running the app.

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a simpler, platform-standard key-value store without native mmap complexity.

alternatives.name: hive_ce
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a pure Dart NoSQL database with strong type adapters.

alternatives.name: flutter_secure_storage
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you strictly need hardware-backed secure storage for sensitive tokens.
